pr_body:
1. implementation of `TextWriter.WriteLineAsync()` corrected The previous implementation differed from the other `TextWriter.*Async` implementations, so that a malfunction with overwritten synchronous methods occurred. As described in #30351.

2. adjustment of the `IndentedTextWriter.Indent` setter, This did not take into account the adjustment of the indent level after executing `writer.Indent++' for example.

Fix #30351

Also, a lot of tests are failing, and there should be new tests added as well for the specific behavior this is fixing.
I can add some tests after the Easter weekend that cover the functionality and bug from the issue.

issue_context.title: IndentedTextWriter Async methods don't indent properly
issue_context.body:
[System.CodeDom.Compiler.IndentedTextWriter](https://github.com/dotnet/corefx/blob/master/src/System.Runtime.Extensions/src/System/CodeDom/Compiler/IndentedTextWriter.cs) wrapped around a `StringWriter` doesn't indent properly when using the `WriteLineAsync` methods.

- First write is not indented
- Writes following empty lines (i.e. from `await WriteLineAsync();`) are not indented
- Lines following lines with content are indented correctly.

Gist: https://gist.github.com/markrendle/01b8b70d2b7c4f023bf196e96562c14a

N.B.: I know there's no point using `*Async` on a `StringWriter`, but the code in question is used with both `StringWriter` and `StreamWriter`.

N.B. 2: I'd just submit a PR to fix this, but I don't know if that would constitute a breaking change.

Using .NET Core 3.0 Preview 7 win-x64.
comments:

Can you please add triple slash documentation for these new public APIs? Once these overrides are published, they will show up with empty documentation in MS Docs.

Right now, we [only see these methods](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.codedom.compiler.indentedtextwriter?view=netcore-3.1) as inherited from TextWriter, so we only see the documentation that was added to TextWriter.

You can base your comments on the original TextWriter comments, and adjust the text for the specific behavior in these methods.
@carlossanlop, we can't just auto-inherit the docs?

Sure, we can auto-inherit, and then port the documentation using the DocsPortingTool (making sure to include inherited documentation from interfaces).
But shouldn't these methods have a slightly different documentation based on the fact that the text is indented?

> But shouldn't these methods have a slightly different documentation based on the fact that the text is indented?

You're right.  It looks like the current overrides do.  Ok.

You can simplify this method by calling the other one and avoid repeated code:
```suggestion
        public override async Task WriteLineAsync(char[] buffer, int index, int count) => WriteLineAsync(buffer.AsMemory(index, count));
```
